To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the meridional transport of heat and salt across two trans- Atlantic sections is mainly driven by the wind and the meridional wind-driven ageostrophic transport is about 2–4 times stronger than the geostrophic transport.
the meridional volume transport across 14.5°N and 11°S is 6.2 and 11.8
the Ekman volume, salt, and heat transports are northward at 15° N and southward at 10° S, in agreement with the wind stress curl.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the meridional transport of heat and salt in the upper ocean of the tropical Atlantic.
the meridional transport of heat and freshwater in the tropical Atlantic, which is of importance to the thermohaline circulation and to the climate.
the meridional transport in the tropical North and South Atlantic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed ageostrophic velocity at the two sections can be interpreted as the Ekman velocity.
the meridional heat and salt flux across the tropical Atlantic are dominated by the Ekman transport and that the Ekman transport itself is dominated by the wind stress.
the Ekman volume, and heat and salt flux estimates based on the observations agree well with the estimates based on wind stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ekman volume, salt, and heat fluxes estimated based on the in situ wind data agree well with the estimates based on the in situ observations of the meridional velocity.
the meridional transport of heat and salt in the tropical North and South Atlantic is dominated by the Ekman transport, which is in the order of 1–2 PW and 0.2–0.4 Sv.
the meridional transport in the tropical North Atlantic is mainly driven by Ekman transport, while the meridional salt transport is mainly driven by the geostrophic flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ekman transport and heat fluxes are large in the tropical Atlantic and that the meridional transport of heat and salt by the Ekman layer is of the same order of magnitude as the geostrophic transports.
the Ekman transport is a key component of the meridional oceanic transport, and the meridional heat transport is dominated by the Ekman heat flux.
the ageostrophic transport can be reliably determined from in situ observations of velocity, temperature, and salinity.
